valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E. Target date Nov 2027, so an investor prices FY2028 (Sep 2028) adjusted EPS. FY2027 adjusted EPS guidance is about $7.25 (+10%); base assumes roughly 10% further growth to $7.95. Native USD listing, no FX or ADR conversion. Adjusted EPS basis, GAAP guidance is about $5.70.

bear.driver: Europe and China weakness persists, FY2028 growth stalls and EPS stays at the FY2027 guide

base.driver: About 5% underlying sales growth, segment EBITA margin near 29%, buybacks of about $2.5B a year, giving about 10% EPS growth again

bull.driver: Orders (up 14%, backlog $8.2B) convert to faster growth and margin expansion

valuation.implied_by_close: At base EPS $7.95 the close implies 19.0x (20.8x FY2027 guided EPS). The published Yahoo mean target of $183.11 (28 analysts, aggregate only) implies 23.0x at base EPS, or EPS $8.72 at 21x. The named-analyst weighted target is unavailable because no call has a documented 12-month horizon.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $7.95 (5.3% of close).
valuation.watch_metric: Underlying orders growth and adjusted segment EBITA margin against the 29% FY2027 guide
valuation.next_disclosure: Fiscal Q1 2027 earnings (expected early Feb 2027), Q1 adjusted EPS guide $1.58-$1.62

analyst_notes: Only two named analysts with dated calls were verifiable: KeyBanc's Ken Newman raised to $200 from $170 (Overweight) the day after the Nov 4 earnings, while Morgan Stanley's Chris Snyder raised to $175 from $140 but stays Underweight. Other post-earnings raises (Citi to $198, BNP Paribas Exane $200, Bernstein $196, RBC $196, Wells Fargo $180, DA Davidson $160) were reported without a verifiable analyst name or documented horizon and are excluded. The sample is too small and has no documented horizon, so the Yahoo aggregate mean of $183.11 (+21%) is the only broad reference; versus the $167 base the gap is about 10.7 pp of upside (21.3% vs 10.6%), equal to about 2 turns of P/E or about $0.77 of EPS at 21x.
